correctness.rationale: The exact generating function f iterated t times equals (t-(t-1)s)/(t+1-ts), giving P(Z_t>=h)=(t+1)^(-1)(t/(t+1))^(h-1) for t>=1. With h=ceil(n(lambda_n+x)), compact rescaled immigration times u=k lambda_n/n yield rare-event mass e^(-x) u^alpha exp(-u)/Gamma(alpha+1)du. Early u and late k tails are bounded using respectively polynomial integrability and an exponentially small e^(-2lambda_n) envelope, so all mass is accounted for. Independent clan indicators and max individual probability o(1) give the marked Poisson limit; unique top marks imply the joint Gumbel/Gamma limit. Exact moments E Z_t=1, Var Z_t=2t prove the aggregate L2 law and maximal-clan share by Slutsky. Boundary alpha>0 and t=0 are handled explicitly. A standalone stdlib checker replayed 3214 finite assertions; the analytical argument, not enumeration, proves the infinite statement.

value.rationale: The natural population genealogy asks which immigration cohort supplies the largest extant family and whether that clan dominates a population with increasing arrival flux. Beyond an aggregate law, the result determines the exact logarithmic correction, complete marked Poisson limit, Gamma immigration-time localization independent of size fluctuation, asymptotic absence of ties, and explicit vanishing-share rate. The early-founder localization at times of order n/log n is not a fixed-slice table calculation and is plausibly relevant to population genealogy and extreme-lineage inference.
